Value at Risk for actuarial losses

Source: R/value_at_risk.R
value_at_risk.Rd

Computes the lower quantile VaR at level p: the smallest x for which F_X(x) >= p. No interpolation across probability atoms; for discrete claims, the quantile is an observed support point, not an interpolated monetary amount.

Usage

value_at_risk(x, level = 0.95, value = NULL)

Arguments

x

A vector of observed losses, a tibble of simulations, a severity specification with an exact quantile, or an [aggregate_distribution()] result. A zero-payment specification is also accepted.

level

Probability levels strictly between zero and one.

value

Optional character name of a loss column in a data frame. By default, `aggregate_loss`, `claim_amount`, `claim_count`, `loss`, or `payment` is selected (in that order).

Value

A tibble with `level`, `value_at_risk`, and `method`.

Details

The tail probability retained by an aggregate-distribution object is never renormalized away. Quantiles in its uncomputed tail are rejected. For sampled losses the definition is empirical, not a model-based claim. FFT count truncation can omit probability at small losses as well as large losses. If the omitted count mass could move the selected quantile to a smaller amount, VaR is rejected; recompute with a smaller `tol`.

Examples

value_at_risk(c(0, 100, 100, 300), level = c(0.5, 0.9))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   level value_at_risk method              
#>   <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>               
#> 1   0.5           100 empirical_simulation
#> 2   0.9           300 empirical_simulation
value_at_risk(severity_spec("exponential", rate = 0.01), level = 0.95)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   level value_at_risk method        
#>   <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>         
#> 1  0.95          300. exact_quantile
